name: receipt-printer

frames.best_why: Receipt hangs fully printed under the head with 'Pull down to tear', showing the whole object.

tagline: A small printer feeds out a paper receipt that you pull until it tears free.
summary: A dark card shaped like a receipt printer. It prints a coffee receipt line by line, then you drag the paper down to rip it off and watch it tumble away.
appearance: A tall dark rounded card with a grey printer head across the top showing a shop name and a status word. Below it a white receipt hangs with a serrated bottom edge, monospace text, dotted dividers and a barcode.
behaviour: When it scrolls into view the receipt feeds out line by line while the head buzzes. Pulling the paper stretches it from the slot, and a sharp drag tears it so it falls and spins out of view; a button prints another.
demo_content: Northside Coffee receipt: flat white, almond croissant, oat milk, banana bread, total $18.58.
search_phrases: paper that tears off and falls
drag paper to rip it off
use_when: A playful order confirmation or checkout flourish, where the printed receipt itself is the reward.
avoid_when: The card is a hard 288px wide and 480px tall, so it will not fit a narrow column or short panel.
customise: Merchant, order number, date, the item array, tax rate and currency symbol are props; the look, feed timing and physics constants live in the file.
weight_why: Fixed-step physics runs at 120 steps a second, but only while printing or falling.

a11y.note: Print and tear have keyboard buttons, but the stretch-and-drag gesture has no keyboard equivalent.

issues: The card has a hardcoded 288px width and 480px height, so it cannot fit narrow columns.
polish_why: Believable print feed, tear and fall; a convincing small object with fine edges.
